newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Kidnapped Papua New Guinea MP released.
newsitem.headline: Kidnapped Papua New Guinea MP released.

text.p: A Papua New Guinea member of parliament kidnapped by separatists on Bougainville Island has been released unharmed, the Papua New Guinea government said on Tuesday.
John Momis, the member for Bougainville in the national parliament, was abducted on Sunday by members of the Bougainville Revolutionary Army, while campaigning for forthcoming elections.
Few details were available, but the government in a statement praised the efforts of Bougainville church and community groups in securing his release.
Momis, a former Roman Catholic priest, is a supporter of the Papua New Guinea government's position on Bougainville, where rebels have been fighting a secessionist war for nine years.
The island came to international attention earlier this year when an army revolt stymied government plans to use merceneries to put an end to the uprising.
Acting Prime Minister John Giheno last week unveiled a surprise plan aimed at peacefully ending the rebellion, in which thousands have died, mainly from disease.
